$comment: TF-C56 + TF-C75 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-TARGET; D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM, CLOSED): bare `char`'s signedness is an (architecture × PLATFORM) fact, and EVERY row below now asserts REAL behaviour — no row in this example pins a defect any more. ONE source; the per-target exitCode IS the witness: `char c = (char)0x80; c < 0` is TRUE→10 wherever bare `char` is SIGNED (x86_64 SysV, x86_64 pe64, AND arm64-DARWIN) and FALSE→20 where it is UNSIGNED (arm64-LINUX — the only unsigned-`char` leg DSS ships). The `volatile` seed keeps the byte a RUNTIME value, so the release arm exercises the real machine char→int extension (sign-extending vs zero-extending byte load) rather than a const-fold. WHY THE TWO arm64 ROWS LEGITIMATELY DISAGREE: C 6.2.5p15 leaves bare-`char` signedness IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED and AAPCS64 leaves it implementation-defined too, so the PLATFORM decides and not the processor — the AArch64/GNU-Linux platform ABI chose UNSIGNED, Apple's arm64 platform ABI chose SIGNED, and clang follows the platform. Signedness is therefore never an architecture property. HOW DSS GETS IT RIGHT (TF-C75): the signedness DSS applies is resolved per (architecture × OBJECT-FORMAT) pair from the target configuration, rather than per architecture — that resolution IS the content of TF-C75. ★ THIS EXAMPLE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RESTATE THE CONFIG KEYS THAT CARRY IT. The declaration has already been reshaped once and may be reshaped again; these rows must keep asserting the same OBSERVABLE behaviour across any such rework, so what they pin is the resolved ANSWER — UNSIGNED on arm64 × elf, SIGNED on every other shipped leg — and never the spelling of the key that produces it. So arm64:macho64 and arm64:elf64 — one CPU, two platforms — return different numbers by design, and the two rows below are exactly that proof. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64 with Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) via /usr/bin/clang, every exit code captured DIRECTLY (never after a pipe): (a) `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null` DEFINES __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1 for -target aarch64-linux-gnu, and does NOT define it for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc or x86_64-apple-darwin; (b) `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` compiles clean (rc 0 ⇒ SIGNED) for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and FAILS (rc 1 ⇒ UNSIGNED) for aarch64-linux-gnu; (c) this example's own exit expression `((char)0x80 < 0 ? 10 : 20)` constant-evaluates to 10 for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and to 20 for aarch64-linux-gnu; (d) on THIS main.c clang emits a SIGN-extending byte load natively on arm64-darwin (ldrsb ×1, ldrb ×0) and a ZERO-extending one under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu (ldrsb ×0, ldrb ×1); (e) THIS main.c, clang-built and run NATIVELY, exits 10 at -O0 AND 10 at -O2. ★ RUNNABILITY ON THIS HOST: only the arm64:macho64 row actually EXECUTES on a darwin host — the runner compiles the other three and then reports that their `runOn` excludes host=darwin. Their expected values rest on the (b)/(c) clang facts above, which are per-PLATFORM-TRIPLE and were re-measured for this cycle.

targets.$comment: ★ THIS 20 IS CORRECT AND ASSERTS REAL BEHAVIOUR — it is NOT a leftover of the defect the macho row below used to pin, and it must NOT be flipped to 10. Bare `char` genuinely IS UNSIGNED on aarch64-linux-gnu, so `(char)0x80 < 0` is FALSE there and this program returns 20. This row is the ONLY unsigned-`char` leg DSS ships, and it is the half of the (architecture × platform) split that makes the split observable at all: arm64:macho64 (10) and arm64:elf64 (20) are the SAME CPU on two platforms, and if both rows ever read the same number this example has stopped testing the thing it exists to test. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 (Apple clang 21.0.0 / clang-2100.1.1.101 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, /usr/bin/clang): `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target aarch64-linux-gnu` DEFINES __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1; `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` FAILS (rc 1 ⇒ unsigned) for that triple; clang emits a ZERO-extending byte load (ldrsb ×0, ldrb ×1) for this file under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu; and this example's exit expression `((char)0x80 < 0 ? 10 : 20)` constant-evaluates to 20 there. DSS reaches the same 20 by CONFIG rather than by accident: arm64 × elf is the one shipped (architecture × object-format) pair the target configuration resolves to UNSIGNED. The RUN itself was not executed on this host (this is a linux/aarch64 image and no qemu-aarch64 is installed here); the 20 rests on the four clang facts just listed.

★ THIS 10 IS CORRECT AND ASSERTS REAL BEHAVIOUR. It was 20 until TF-C75, pinned there as the closing witness for D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM — a silent wrong-value miscompile in which DSS zero-extended a negative bare `char` on macho-arm64 where clang sign-extends. THAT ANCHOR IS NOW CLOSED and this row was flipped 20 → 10 as the proof; the history is kept here only so a future reader knows why this row carries a comment at all. Bare `char` is SIGNED on arm64-apple-darwin, so `(char)0x80 < 0` is TRUE and the program returns 10 — the same answer as the two x86_64 rows, and deliberately DIFFERENT from the arm64:elf64 row above. WHAT MAKES IT 10 IN DSS: the target configuration resolves the arm64 × macho pair to SIGNED, overriding the AArch64 CPU default of unsigned (which is correct only for linux-arm64). Make the configuration resolve this pair to unsigned again — by whatever key currently carries the platform half — and this row silently returns 20 with no diagnostic, which is precisely the regression it exists to catch. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, every exit code captured DIRECTLY (never after a pipe): Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) compiled this exact main.c and ran it natively → exit 10 at -O0 AND exit 10 at -O2; DSS compiled the same file for arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec and ran it → exit 10 in the baseline arm AND exit 10 under the `release` arm. Same host, same source, same target, 10 four ways — DSS and clang agree. Do NOT delete this row, do NOT relax it to accept either value, and do NOT drop the macho leg: a failure here now means a REGRESSION (the format key lost, or the resolution order inverted), not a known defect. ★ STANDING CONSTRAINT (carried forward, reason rewritten): do not build a runtime ARCHITECTURE cross-check on bare-`char` signedness in other corpus examples. The original reason — that such a test would go green by agreeing with this defect — is obsolete. The reason it still holds is that `char` signedness is NOT an architecture fact at all: it is (architecture × platform), so any example using it to identify a CPU asserts something untrue and breaks on the next platform added for that CPU. The one legitimate consumer is examples/c-subset/char_signedness_macro_coherence, which uses it to cross-check two DECLARATIONS of the same fact rather than to identify a machine.
